text.p: Israeli bonds rose broadly on Monday, led by a rise in unlinked bonds in dull trading, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.11 pct to 104.11
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.11 to 103.27
Volume was a low 92 million shekels.
"Activity was low today with most of it concentrated in unlinked bonds. CPI-linked bonds closed higher today, led by a rise in short bonds," said one trader.
"The rate decision was not surprising and it had no impact on trading," he said.
The Bank of Israel said on Sunday it was holding its key lending rate for April at an annualised 13.9 percent.
"Inflation-linked bonds rose slightly but they are very stable now. They made a big move since the beginning of the year and now they need to rest," said Ron Wiesberg at I.B.I. Investment House.

"Yields on CPI-linked bonds fell sharply and investors are more interested now in unlinked bonds which offer yields of 14.4 percent, which is very attractive for investors who believe that inflation will remain under control in coming months," Weisberg added.
Traders said that Makams, which are also unlinked, also rose, but on a very low volume of only 27 million shekels.
Dollar linked bonds closed slightly higher in very thin trading.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
